content.rendered:
Block Board, also known as solid core plywood, is a high-strength, lightweight, and durable engineered wood product widely used in furniture, doors, cabinets, and interior construction. It combines the stability of solid wood with the versatility of plywood, making it ideal for modern woodworking and building projects.

Composition

  • Core: Solid softwood strips (usually poplar or pine) arranged edge-to-edge and glued together.

  • Facing: Thin layers of high-quality hardwood veneer on both sides, providing a smooth and attractive surface suitable for finishing.

Types

  • Standard Block Board: Suitable for general furniture and interior construction.

  • Moisture-Resistant Block Board: Treated for humid areas such as kitchens and bathrooms.

  • Fire-Retardant Block Board: Enhanced with additives to improve fire resistance.

  • Custom Veneer Boards: Available with various hardwood veneers for decorative applications.

Key Features

  • Lightweight yet strong, ideal for long spans without sagging.

  • Smooth, attractive surface ready for painting, laminating, or veneering.

  • Easy to cut, shape, and assemble using standard woodworking tools.

  • Resistant to warping and cracking compared to solid wood.

  • Eco-friendly option using sustainable wood strips and veneers.

Installation & Usage

  • Widely used in furniture making, door panels, partitions, cabinets, and interior wall paneling.

  • Can be laminated, veneered, or polished according to design requirements.

Advantages

  • Combines the strength of solid wood with the lightweight of plywood.

  • Cost-effective alternative to solid wood.

  • Versatile and durable, suitable for both decorative and structural applications.

Limitations

  • Not completely waterproof unless treated.

  • Requires proper handling to avoid surface scratches.

title.rendered: Oriented Strand Board: Structural Strength Meets Versatility

content.rendered:
OSB (Oriented Strand Board) is a type of engineered wood panel, considered an upgraded form of particle board. It is manufactured from long wood strands (larger than those used in conventional particle board, typically 75–150 mm long, 10–25 mm wide, and 0.5–0.7 mm thick). These strands are oriented in specific directions, bonded with adhesives (commonly phenolic resin or MDI resin), and hot-pressed under high temperature and pressure to form a structural panel.

Key Features

  • High Strength: The wood strands are oriented — the surface layers are aligned along the panel’s length, while the core layer is arranged crosswise. This gives OSB mechanical properties close to plywood and higher load-bearing capacity than conventional particle board.

  • Good Stability: Resistant to cracking and warping, with strong screw-holding capacity.

  • Large Panel Size: Common size is 1220 × 2440 mm, which allows whole-panel applications and reduces joints.

  • Environmental Performance: Typically uses formaldehyde-free adhesives (MDI resin), with much lower formaldehyde emissions compared to particle board or MDF.

Applications

  • Construction: Formwork, roofing, wall sheathing, subflooring.

  • Furniture: Wardrobes, cabinets, countertop substrates.

  • Packaging: Pallets, packing boxes.

content.rendered:
Block Board, also known as solid core plywood, is a high-strength, lightweight, and durable engineered wood product widely used in furniture, doors, cabinets, and interior construction. It combines the stability of solid wood with the versatility of plywood, making it ideal for modern woodworking and building projects.

Composition

  • Core: Solid softwood strips (usually poplar or pine) arranged edge-to-edge and glued together.

  • Facing: Thin layers of high-quality hardwood veneer on both sides, providing a smooth and attractive surface suitable for finishing.

Types

  • Standard Block Board: Suitable for general furniture and interior construction.

  • Moisture-Resistant Block Board: Treated for humid areas such as kitchens and bathrooms.

  • Fire-Retardant Block Board: Enhanced with additives to improve fire resistance.

  • Custom Veneer Boards: Available with various hardwood veneers for decorative applications.

Key Features

  • Lightweight yet strong, ideal for long spans without sagging.

  • Smooth, attractive surface ready for painting, laminating, or veneering.

  • Easy to cut, shape, and assemble using standard woodworking tools.

  • Resistant to warping and cracking compared to solid wood.

  • Eco-friendly option using sustainable wood strips and veneers.

Installation & Usage

  • Widely used in furniture making, door panels, partitions, cabinets, and interior wall paneling.

  • Can be laminated, veneered, or polished according to design requirements.

Advantages

  • Combines the strength of solid wood with the lightweight of plywood.

  • Cost-effective alternative to solid wood.

  • Versatile and durable, suitable for both decorative and structural applications.

Limitations

  • Not completely waterproof unless treated.

  • Requires proper handling to avoid surface scratches.

Bailing Melamine Plywood: The Premier Choice for Modern Interiors

Bailing Melamine Plywood is a high-performance, ready-to-use engineered wood panel designed for efficiency, durability, and style. By fusing a decorative melamine paper laminate onto a robust, first-class poplar core, this plywood delivers a flawless surface ideal for a wide range of commercial and residential applications. It is the smart, cost-effective solution for builders, manufacturers, and designers seeking quality and value.

Key Features & Benefits

  • Exceptional Durability: The hard, polished melamine surface provides outstanding resistance to scratches, moisture, stains, and daily wear and tear. It ensures long-lasting beauty and is remarkably easy to clean and maintain.

  • Ready-to-Use Efficiency: Pre-finished with a double-sided decorative surface, our plywood arrives on-site ready for fabrication. This eliminates the need for additional painting or laminating, saving significant time, labor, and material costs.

  • Eco-Conscious Design: We prioritize environmental responsibility. Our panels are engineered with eco-friendly processes and comply with recognized Formaldehyde Emission Standards (E2), contributing to healthier indoor environments.

  • Superior Stability: Constructed with a FIRST-CLASS poplar core and balanced double-sided decoration, the panel offers excellent dimensional stability, resisting warping and bending for reliable performance.

  • Modern Aesthetics: Available in a contemporary style with a consistent, polished finish, it provides a sleek and professional look perfect for modern office furniture, cabinetry, and interior projects.

Hard Board, also known as high-density fiberboard (HDF) or fiber hardboard, is a durable, dense, and versatile engineered wood product widely used in construction, furniture, and decorative applications. It combines strength, smooth surface finish, and resistance to wear, making it ideal for both structural and decorative uses.

Composition

  • Made from wood fibers or recycled wood, bonded with resins under high pressure and temperature.

  • Produces a dense, rigid board with a smooth surface suitable for painting, laminating, or veneering.

Types

  • Standard Hard Board: General-purpose applications in furniture and wall panels.

  • Moisture-Resistant Hard Board: Enhanced to withstand humid conditions, suitable for kitchens or bathrooms.

  • Fire-Retardant Hard Board: Treated to resist fire for safety-sensitive installations.

  • Decorative Hard Board: Laminated or veneered for aesthetic applications.

Key Features

  • High density and strength, capable of withstanding pressure and impact.

  • Smooth and uniform surface, ready for finishing or laminating.

  • Moisture, termite, and fire-resistant (depending on type).

  • Lightweight and easy to cut, shape, and install.

  • Eco-friendly: Can be made from recycled wood fibers.

Installation & Usage

  • Commonly used for furniture backing, wall panels, flooring underlayment, partition boards, and decorative panels.

  • Can be painted, laminated, or veneered for customized finishes.

Advantages

  • Strong, durable, and versatile for multiple applications.

  • Smooth surface suitable for painting or laminating.

  • Cost-effective and environmentally friendly.

Limitations

  • Not completely waterproof unless treated.

  • Cutting or machining produces fine dust; protective equipment recommended.

Cement Board, also known as fiber cement board or backer board, is a durable and high-performance building material widely used for wall, floor, and ceiling applications, especially in wet or high-moisture areas. It offers superior strength, fire resistance, and moisture protection compared to traditional gypsum boards.

Composition

  • Core: Made from cement, sand, and reinforcing fibers (such as cellulose or glass fibers), forming a rigid and durable board.

  • Surface: Smooth or textured surfaces suitable for tiling, painting, or other finishes.

Types

  • Standard Cement Board: Suitable for interior walls and ceilings.

  • Waterproof / Moisture-Resistant Board: Ideal for bathrooms, kitchens, and exterior applications.

  • Fire-Resistant Board: Enhanced for applications requiring high fire protection.

  • Tile Backer Board: Designed as a base for ceramic, stone, or porcelain tile installation.

Key Features

  • Waterproof and moisture-resistant, preventing mold and decay.

  • High impact and load-bearing strength.

  • Fire-resistant and non-combustible.

  • Pest-resistant: Does not attract termites or other insects.

  • Can be cut and installed easily using standard construction tools.

  • Compatible with tile, stone, or decorative finishes.

Installation

  • Fixed to metal or wooden studs with cement board screws.

  • Joints sealed with waterproof tape and thin-set mortar for a smooth, moisture-proof finish.

Advantages

  • Ideal for wet areas like bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms.

  • Durable and long-lasting: Resistant to water, mold, and fire.

  • Supports tile and stone installations without sagging.

  • Cost-effective and easy to maintain.

Limitations

  • Heavier than gypsum board, requiring sturdy framing.

  • Cutting may produce dust; protective gear is recommended.

Gypsum Board, also known as drywall, plasterboard, or wallboard, is a versatile and widely used building material for interior walls and ceilings. It combines strength, fire resistance, and ease of installation, making it an ideal solution for modern construction.

Composition

  • Core: Made of high-quality gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O), providing rigidity and excellent fire resistance.

  • Facing: Sandwiched between layers of thick paper (usually recycled), offering a smooth surface ready for painting or finishing.

Types

  • Standard Gypsum Board: Ideal for general wall and ceiling applications.

  • Moisture-Resistant (Green Board): Designed for humid areas like bathrooms and kitchens.

  • Fire-Resistant (Type X): Enhanced with additives to resist fire, perfect for commercial or multi-story buildings.

  • Soundproofing Board: Thicker or denser panels to reduce noise transmission.

Key Features

  • Lightweight and easy to cut and install.

  • Smooth surface suitable for painting, wallpapering, or decorative finishes.

  • Large panel sizes for efficient installation: 4 ft × 8 ft (1.2 m × 2.4 m).

  • Fire-resistant: Gypsum’s water content releases steam during high heat, slowing fire spread.

Installation

  • Secure to metal or wooden studs using screws or nails.

  • Tape and cover joints with compound to achieve a seamless finish.

Advantages

  • Faster installation than traditional plaster walls.

  • Cost-effective and widely available.

  • Provides fire resistance and, depending on type, sound insulation.

Limitations

  • Not suitable for prolonged water exposure unless moisture-resistant.

  • Less impact-resistant compared to some alternative wall materials.

OSB (Oriented Strand Board) is a type of engineered wood panel, considered an upgraded form of particle board. It is manufactured from long wood strands (larger than those used in conventional particle board, typically 75–150 mm long, 10–25 mm wide, and 0.5–0.7 mm thick). These strands are oriented in specific directions, bonded with adhesives (commonly phenolic resin or MDI resin), and hot-pressed under high temperature and pressure to form a structural panel.

Key Features

  • High Strength: The wood strands are oriented — the surface layers are aligned along the panel’s length, while the core layer is arranged crosswise. This gives OSB mechanical properties close to plywood and higher load-bearing capacity than conventional particle board.

  • Good Stability: Resistant to cracking and warping, with strong screw-holding capacity.

  • Large Panel Size: Common size is 1220 × 2440 mm, which allows whole-panel applications and reduces joints.

  • Environmental Performance: Typically uses formaldehyde-free adhesives (MDI resin), with much lower formaldehyde emissions compared to particle board or MDF.

Applications

  • Construction: Formwork, roofing, wall sheathing, subflooring.

  • Furniture: Wardrobes, cabinets, countertop substrates.

  • Packaging: Pallets, packing boxes.

SPC Flooring Description

SPC (Stone Plastic Composite) Flooring is a high-performance, modern flooring solution designed for both residential and commercial indoor spaces, such as hotels, offices, and homes. Made from a combination of limestone, PVC, and stabilizers, SPC flooring provides excellent durability, water resistance, and fire resistance, making it ideal for high-traffic areas and spaces exposed to moisture.

This flooring features click-lock installation, allowing for easy and secure assembly without the need for adhesives. The surface comes in various textures—including glossy, high gloss, embossed, matte, and hand-scraped finishes—to replicate the natural beauty of wood while providing superior wear resistance (AC3 grade). SPC flooring is available in a variety of plank widths, thicknesses (4–8.5 mm), wear layers (0.2–0.5 mm), sizes, and wood designs, offering flexibility to suit diverse interior design styles.

Key Features and Advantages:

  • Waterproof and Fire-Resistant: Ideal for kitchens, bathrooms, and high-traffic commercial areas.

  • Durable and Wear-Resistant: AC3 wear layer ensures long-lasting performance.

  • Easy Installation: Click-lock system simplifies DIY installation.

  • Variety of Designs: Realistic wood patterns and textures for a modern aesthetic.

  • Low Maintenance: Simple cleaning and no need for polishing or waxing.

With its combination of durability, waterproof performance, and stylish modern design, SPC Flooring is a versatile choice for creating elegant and practical indoor environments.

Commercial Plywood is an excellent choice for builders, designers, and furniture manufacturers seeking a dependable, high-quality, and budget-friendly wood panel solution.

Melamine Particle Board Description

Melamine Particle Board is a high-quality engineered wood product commonly used in modern interior design and furniture manufacturing. It is made by bonding wood particles (such as poplar or hardwood) with resins under high temperature and pressure, and then laminated with a decorative melamine paper surface. This process creates a durable, smooth, and stylish finish that requires no additional painting or coating.

With a density of 600–700 kg/m³ and thickness options ranging from 9–25 mm, Melamine Particle Boards are available in standard sizes such as 1220×2440 mm and 1250×2500 mm. The melamine surface is resistant to scratches, moisture, stains, and heat, making it ideal for use in kitchen cabinets, wardrobes, shelving, office furniture, and home decoration projects.

  • Durable Surface: Scratch-resistant, moisture-proof, and easy to clean.

  • Aesthetic Variety: Available in numerous colors, patterns, and textures to match different interior styles.

  • Cost-Effective: Offers the look of premium finishes at a more affordable price.

  • Eco-Friendly Options: Meets standards like CARB, FSC, and ISO9001, with low formaldehyde emissions (E1/E2 grades).

  • Versatile Applications: Perfect for house decoration, kitchen cabinets, office partitions, and modern furniture.

Melamine Particle Board combines strength, functionality, and contemporary design, making it a preferred material for both residential and commercial projects.

Hollow Particle Board Description

Hollow Particle Board is a modern engineered wood product that construction and furniture manufacturing industries widely use. People know it for its lightweight hollow structure, smooth surface, and reliable strength. Manufacturers primarily make the board from poplar, pine, or mixed wood cores and produce it through high-temperature pressing with eco-friendly adhesives such as MR, E0, E1, E2, or melamine glue. Its finely finished surface provides a sleek and uniform appearance, making it suitable for a wide range of decorative applications.

The typical density ranges from 600–700 kg/cbm, with thickness options of 28–40 mm and standard sizes like 1220×2440 mm and 1830×2440 mm. The hollow structure reduces overall weight while maintaining excellent structural stability and load-bearing capacity, making it ideal for use in furniture, doors, interior partitions, and decorative projects.

Key Advantages of Hollow Particle Board:

  • Lightweight Design: The hollow core significantly reduces weight, simplifying handling, transport, and installation.

  • Strength and Stability: Its engineered composition ensures durability and dependable performance.

  • Eco-Friendly Options: Low formaldehyde emission grades (E0, E1) meet green building and health standards.

  • Versatile Aesthetics: Smooth surfaces are perfect for veneering, laminating, painting, or other surface finishes.

With its modern style, cost-effectiveness, and excellent workability, Hollow Particle Board is an ideal material for contemporary home furniture, interior decoration, and architectural solutions.
